answer_1.quote: LLM planning evaluates performance in embodied environments, while CoScript, TravelPlanner, and PPNL focus on planning problems with constraints.
answer_1.outputs: plans in natural language, PDDL, Pythonic code, symbolic representations

answer_2.quote: Performance criteria are measured using specific metrics: (1) Completeness: success rate and goal condition recall... (2) Executability: executability rate... (3) Optimality: measured by the optimality rate... (4) Efficiency: common metrics include inference time, input and output token counts... (5) Representation: the number of parseable problems... (6) Generalization: all these metrics can also be applied to unseen scenarios...

answer_3.quote: The final evaluation method, LLM-as-a-Judge, uses another LLM to automatically assess the quality of generated plans in the cases mentioned above.

answer_4.quote: The second evaluation method is human evaluation, typically used in the following cases: (1) No available verifier... (2) Open-ended problems... tasks with ambiguous instructions or generative outputs (e.g., text or images) where multiple valid solutions may differ from the ground truth.
answer_4.guideline: Human evaluation is used when there is no automated verifier or for open-ended problems with ambiguous instructions or generative outputs.
